title: finding(i18n): check-i18n-dead-keys sweeps the working tree without excluding `.objectui-tmp`, so it races the CLI tsc-gate test's scratch directory and grep reports ENOENT
body:
`check-i18n-dead-keys` sweeps the whole working tree with a filesystem `grep -rFn`, and its skip set omits `.objectui-tmp` — the directory a CLI test creates and deletes inside the same shard. The sweep descends into that live scratch directory and races its teardown.

Observed on `Test (shard 1/4)`:

```
scripts/check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs:616
grep: …/.objectui-tmp/tsc-gate-3853-1W87E5/tsconfig.json: No such file or directory
```

## Both halves, measured on `origin/main`

**Consumer.** `scripts/check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs` builds the sweep at lines 606-612 and runs it at 616:

```
const args = [
  '-rFn', '-I',
  ...[...TEXT_SWEEP_SKIP_DIRS].flatMap((dir) => ['--exclude-dir', dir]),
  '-f', patternsFile,
  '--', root,
];
output = execFileSync('grep', args, { ... });
```

`TEXT_SWEEP_SKIP_DIRS` (same file, lines 428-431) is `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage`, `.next`, `.turbo`, `.changeset`. **`.objectui-tmp` is not in it** — `grep -c 'objectui-tmp' scripts/check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs` returns `0`.

**Producer.** `packages/cli/src/__tests__/app-generator.test.ts`, in `withGeneratedApp` (lines 1386-1396):

```
const parent = join(REPO_ROOT, '.objectui-tmp');
mkdirSync(parent, { recursive: true });
const dir = mkdtempSync(join(parent, 'tsc-gate-3853-'));
try { write(dir); run(dir); } finally { rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
```

It writes a generated app — `tsconfig.json` among its files — under the repository root and removes it in a `finally`. The directory therefore exists for exactly the span of one test, inside the same shard the sweep runs in.

**Convention control, lit.** The sibling whole-tree sweep already excludes it: `scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` line 246 lists `.objectui-tmp` in its skip set, and its header explains the reason (the directory is written by tooling and holds no source). So the exclusion is an established convention in this tree that exactly one of the two sweeps is missing.

## Why this is not a flake

The interleaving is what varies; the defect does not. A whole-tree `grep -rFn` that is not told to skip a scratch directory will read whatever is in it, and a scratch directory that is being deleted will hand it `ENOENT`. Nothing about the outcome is probabilistic once the two overlap — only whether they overlap is. Calling it a flake would predict it stops on retry, which is a prediction about scheduling, not about either program.

`.objectui-tmp` is `.gitignore`d (`.gitignore:50`), so this is invisible to every `git grep`-based tool in the tree and only the filesystem sweep can see it.

## Suggested direction, not a decision

Adding `.objectui-tmp` to `TEXT_SWEEP_SKIP_DIRS` matches the sibling sweep and costs nothing — nothing under it is source. Whether the two skip sets should instead be derived from one place is a larger question and is deliberately left open here. There may also be other whole-tree sweeps with the same omission; this card records the one that was observed and does not claim to have surveyed them.

## Provenance

Found while working objectui#8937 / PR objectui#9195, as a second annotation on the same shard. It is not caused by that branch: the diff there touches neither this script, nor the CLI test, nor `.gitignore`. That branch does add a test that shells out to `git grep`, and `git grep` reads tracked files only — `.objectui-tmp` is ignored and therefore untracked, so it is never opened by it, and a read cannot create the directory in the first place. The error also names a different grep in a different process.
